data.title: Earwax Removal in Salisbury, NC
data.summary: Even though most of us would prefer not to have earwax, it can be quite helpful in moderate amounts.

children.text: Even though most of us would prefer not to have earwax, it can be quite helpful in moderate amounts. As it travels from the interior of the ear canal outside, collecting dirt, hair, dead skin cells, and debris along the way, it acts as a natural ear cleaner.
Earwax possesses antibacterial and antifungal qualities, according to some studies. In fact, your ears are probably going to feel itchy or uncomfortable if there isn’t enough earwax in them.
However, having too much earwax to the point of impaction or obstruction is another story. In this case, you will need to see an audiologist for professional earwax removal.
What is earwax?

Earwax is a natural secretion that comes from some glands in your ear canal. It can be compared to a gland that produces sweat, so basically, earwax can be likened to ear sweat. Some people aren’t born with glands that produce earwax which causes itchiness in the ears. Put simply, earwax is an important, natural occurrence in the ear.
Why is earwax removal important?
Excess earwax may affect your hearing and may also cause difficulties or physical obstruction during ear check-ups.

Earwax can trigger or cause problems with hearing aids. Why? It’s because earwax is designed to be drawn out from the ears. When you’re wearing hearing aids, you’re basically putting something in your ear which traps or obstructs the natural flow of the earwax.

This is why it is very important to see us regularly. We remove the earwax using sterile tools and proper techniques. Not all hearing healthcare providers are equipped to perform earwax removal, so you need to be very careful in choosing the right hearing care provider.
Can you remove ear wax at home?

Earwax removal can be done at home. There are numerous ear drops or earwax removal kits available at major drugstores. However, we do not really encourage earwax removal at home. Why? It’s because you can’t really see what’s going on inside your ear and it may actually do more harm than good. Also, in the event that you have excessive or occluded earwax, it is much better to see us so not to aggravate the situation.
How do you know if you have earwax build up?

Some people can sense or feel that they have an earwax buildup. People with excessive earwax build-up are most likely to experience a feeling of occlusion, a sensation of fullness in the ears, pain, discomfort and/or itchiness inside the ears.
Is hydrogen peroxide safe?

Hearing healthcare professionals would never recommend pure hydrogen peroxide in the ear canal. One reason is that hydrogen peroxide has a drying agent, so it can really dry the skin. Dryness inside the ears can lead to itchiness.

You might notice that most over-the-counter earwax removal products are peroxide based, however, they are diluted. Never put pure or undiluted hydrogen peroxide in your ears. If you’re planning to do so, you might as well use over-the-counter earwax removal kits.
Can you use cotton swabs to remove earwax?

Medical professionals never recommend inserting a Q-tip into the ear canal. When you do that, you might see some evidence or discoloration on the Q-tip. Looking at the discharge or earwax you might think that you have successfully removed the earwax.

However, it doesn’t really work that way. You are actually pushing the earwax or debris further down into the ear canal. By doing so, the little hairs that line the ear canal can’t do their job. They help move the earwax outward. But when the little hairs are packed with earwax, they don’t work properly.

If you really want to use Q-tips or cotton buds, you can use them on the outer part of the ear, like the bowl of the ear, the ridges, or the pinna. Again, inserting cotton swabs in the ear canal is highly discouraged.
Is earwax removal painful?

Earwax removal is generally painless. There’s no need for painkillers or anesthesia. To avoid harming the ear canal, it’s crucial to remain still throughout the procedure. We use a variety of different methods to remove earwax and will choose the best method depending on your individual needs.
Can earwax cause tinnitus or be mistaken for tinnitus?
Excessive earwax can lead to tinnitus. This happens when excessive earwax is trapped right against the eardrum. Fortunately, this type of tinnitus can be addressed by professional earwax removal.
If the blocked earwax has already been eliminated but you are still suffering from tinnitus, more tests might be required to determine the cause of your tinnitus.

data.summary: With proper care and maintenance, hearing aids can be long-lasting devices that work effectively for several years.

children.text: With proper care and maintenance, hearing aids can be long-lasting devices that work effectively for several years.

Hearing aids are a major investment in your overall health. These devices offer critical support that helps you move through daily life with greater ease and comfort. Hearing aid repairs and professional maintenance are integral in ensuring that your hearing aids are in good, functional condition for a long time.
Because they can be impacted by normal daily wear and tear, it is important to know and practice ways to best care for your devices. If you do face issues with your hearing aids, we are here to help!
Hearing Solutions of North Carolina provides professional hearing aid repair services in Salisbury, NC and nearby locations.
Hearing Aid Repair and Troubleshooting
All
hearing aid

devices consist of the main components which are: microphone, receiver (or speaker), amplifier, and battery source. These parts are built into the device and can be impacted by various factors over time. You will be able to identify when your device seems to be malfunctioning or not working as well. Before bringing your device to our office for hearing aid repair, you can try to troubleshoot at home. A few useful ways to troubleshoot the most common hearing aids issues include:
check your device

Fully inspect your device. Specifically check for anything that could be blocking sound from entering into the microphones or exiting the receiver. Obstructions to sound can include earwax, hair, dirt, moisture build up etc. Thoroughly remove any debris that has accumulated on your device and thoroughly clean your hearing aid.
Turn up the Volume
Make sure the volume is turned on and set to meet your specific settings. The volume could have been accidentally turned down or off which impacts your ability to hear.
change the batteries

There are two types of batteries that power hearing aids: disposable batteries, lithium ion batteries. Check the batteries to ensure that they are positioned correctly in the battery compartment. Swap out the batteries for new ones if needed. Check to be sure your rechargeable device has been properly inserted into the charger and that the charger is free of lint or debris.
inspect the tubing

Several hearing aid styles feature a small tube that connects the device’s components. Inspect this tube for any damage: cracks, holes, breakage, moisture, etc. This will need to be repaired professionally.

If you have tried these troubleshooting strategies or reviewed our cleaning videos listed under the resources tab and continue to have issues with your device, contact us at Hearing Solutions of North Carolina. We will check your device for any necessary hearing aid repair or adjsutments.
When to Seek Professional Hearing Aid Repair Services
Hearing aids are highly durable devices that typically last from 4-5 years. It is normal to need hearing aid repair services over this long duration because the devices are worn and used daily.
There are a few factors that indicate your device needs professional repair services. This can include the following:
Feedback
You experience unpleasant feedback and other types of noise that reduce sound quality and prevent you from hearing clearly and comfortably.
Visible Damage
There is noticeable damage anywhere on the device – cracks, tears, holes, the battery door does not close properly etc.
Short Batter Life

Batteries are not powering your hearing aid for as long as they have previously. Even when you switch to new batteries or continue to place your device in the charger, your device doesn’t hold charge for the same amount of time.
Fortunately, we provide professional hearing aid repair services in our office!
This allows you to bring your device in and have us repair it conveniently and relatively quickly.
Contact us today at Hearing Solutions of North Carolina for more information on our hearing aid repair services.
Preventing Hearing Aid Repairs
It is important to practice all the ways to best care for your hearing aids. Consistent maintenance supports the longevity and quality of your device. A few tips to practice include:
1. Clean Device Daily:

It can be easy for your hearing aids to be impacted by natural debris that buildup in the ears. This includes earwax, dirt, hair etc. which then land on the device and this can contribute to malfunctioning hearing aid components. So, it is important to thoroughly clean your device daily. You should have a routine that you easily perform when you remove your hearing aids at night. This should include using a cloth or dry tissue to remove anything that has accumulated on your device throughout the day and brushing the receiver with the toothbrush provided the day you were fit with your new hearing aids.
2. Clean Your Ears

In addition to cleaning your device, it is important to also clean your ears. Removing excess earwax, moisture, and other natural elements that can accumulate in the ear canal is an integral way to also keep your hearing aids clean. Avoid using cotton swabs to clean your ears and opt for a washcloth or using other methods like ear irrigation. We will always look into your ears during your maintenance checks and remove any wax we can.
3. Keep Your Hearing Aid Dry

Moisture can easily damage hearing aids so keeping your devices as dry as possible is important. You should remove your devices before showering, swimming, or engaging in any other activity that exposes you to excess water. If needed, we carry dehumidifiers that are safe for your hearing aids. Before reinserting your hearing aids, make sure that your ears are thoroughly dry!

data.title: Hearing Health FAQs
data.summary: At Hearing Solutions of North Carolina, we take a proactive approach to providing hearing healthcare to our patients.

children.text: At Hearing Solutions of North Carolina, we take a proactive approach to providing hearing healthcare to our patients. On top of our best practices, state-of-the-art equipment, and experienced
audiologists
, we see to it that we educate our patients by addressing their queries and concerns related to hearing care.
During consultations, we encourage and welcome hearing questions and answers to ensure that our patients understand and appreciate our process of providing hearing healthcare.
Check out our curated hearing health FAQs below:
How do I protect my hearing?

Changes in hearing ability have many different causes and sometimes it cannot always be avoided. However, the good news is that there are fundamental things you can do to ensure that your hearing health is a priority and that precautionary measures are taken.
Limit your noise exposure and protect your hearing when in loud environments.
Get annual hearing tests so that you can monitor your hearing health and take action as soon as any changes occur.
Maintain a healthy lifestyle including exercise and proper diet.
Avoid nicotine use.
Do changes in hearing ability only affect older people?

People of all ages can experience changes in hearing ability, however the average age is over 65 years old. There are 6 million individuals with hearing difficulties in the US between the ages of 18-44. The World Health Organization has reported the rise of cases among younger people, in no small part due to the widespread use of smartphones and earbuds!
Would my primary care physician check my hearing?

Only 13% of doctors routinely check their patient's hearing. Many people find it more difficult to hear in noisy situations. Therefore, in quiet environments like a doctor's office, most people can hear just fine, so it can be challenging for your PCP to recognize hearing difficulties. As such, it is important to include a
hearing evaluation
in your annual healthcare checkups.
Does hearing loss cause tinnitus?

While tinnitus and decreases in hearing ability are often experienced simultaneously, one does not cause the other. Research suggests that both tinnitus and changes in hearing share the same root causes (often the damage of inner ear cells), so it's not surprising they often show up together. Tinnitus and hearing difficulties are both treatable - contact us to learn more!
Can hearing be improved?

This question never fails to make it to our hearing health FAQs list. It really depends on the cause of the hearing difficulty. In some instances, hearing challenges caused by blockages or impacted earwax can be “cured” once the blockages are removed. Sometimes surgery can be done to correct medical problems in the outer or middle ear.

However, sensorineural hearing loss is by far more common. There are many causes including medical conditions, age-related and noise-induced hearing loss to name a few. The delicate hair cells in the inner ear are unable to repair themselves which results in certain sounds and frequencies no longer within your hearing range. The most common solution is to amplify those sounds putting them back into your hearing range.
Can hearing devices completely fix my hearing?
" I need hearing aids. Now what?"
If you have been diagnosed with hearing loss, one of the first recommendations would be to get a hearing aid.
Hearing aids
help you interact with the world around you, but they do not "fix" your hearing, just as your nearsightedness or farsightedness is not fixed when wearing glasses.
Think of hearing devices as a solution that supports all aspects of your life!
Do I need two hearing aids?
This is another popular hearing aids FAQ. Some of our patients ask, "Do hearing aids come in pairs?"

Before getting to the answer, you need to understand that human hearing is binaural. This means that we pick up sounds with both of our ears. While unilateral issues do exist (in one ear), binaural issues are far more common. Binaural hearing loss is treated with the use of two hearing aids. When it comes to hearing, it is important to have a comprehensive hearing test that accurately determines your hearing abilities. We’re here to help you find the best solution for your needs.
Why are hearing devices so expensive?

Hearing devices are advanced, sophisticated electronic devices that embody decades of research and technological innovation. Moreover, they are an incredibly important investment in your overall health and well-being. Indeed, their value far exceeds the investment.. And there are good reasons for this.

Hundreds of millions of dollars are spent annually by the hearing industry to move hearing technology forward. And it has worked - the latest hearing devices use artificial technology, motion sensors, and directional microphones to improve the listening experience like never before.

In addition to your investment in the technology you are also investing in your hearing healthcare team of providers to ensure that the best devices were chosen for you, that they are properly programmed and verification measures are completed to confirm proper programming. Ongoing care and maintenance is a vital part of your investment so you know you are hearing and understanding the best you can for years to come.
Should I avoid buying hearing aids online?

It is tempting to think that it is sufficient to choose the right hearing aid to guarantee a good hearing aid experience. For that reason, many individuals believe that hearing aids are all more or less the same, so they shop around and are very price-sensitive.

At Hearing Solutions of North Carolina, we ensure that you are fitted with the best hearing aids for your specific hearing needs. With our lifestyle-focused consultation and state-of-the-art technology, our expertise translates to the best listening experience for you. Additionally, we verify your devices using live speech mapping and fine-tune the programming to ensure your unique needs are met.

While online hearing aids may seem like a convenient and simple solution, it is important to remember that your hearing health is an integral part of your overall health and well-being. That’s why we provide ongoing service and peace of mind support, such as fittings, adjustments, repair, and device maintenance. This ensures the best experience and optimal results with your devices.
Are cheap hearing aids worth buying?

While some cheap hearing aids may be worth a try for certain individuals, others may require more advanced or powerful hearing aids to address their specific hearing loss. When considering a hearing aid, it's important to consult with an audiologist who can perform a comprehensive hearing evaluation and make recommendations based on your unique hearing needs. Audiologists may also be able to help you navigate the options available at various price points.
Can you self-refer to an audiologist?

In most cases, you can self-refer to an audiologist. This simply means that you can make an appointment with an audiologist without a referral from a healthcare provider. However, it's important to check with your insurance provider to see if they require a referral before they will cover the cost of your visit. Some insurance plans may also have specific audiologists accredited, so it's a good idea to check with your insurance provider to find out which audiologists are covered under your plan.
How can I tell if my hearing is bad?
Have you been noticing some red flags in your hearing health lately? Below are several signs that may indicate that you have hearing loss:
Difficulty hearing conversations, especially in noisy environments.
Turning up the volume on the radio or TV louder than others in the same room would prefer.
Struggling to understand soft or low-volume speech.
Finding it challenging to hear high-pitched sounds like a child/woman’s voice.

If you are experiencing any of these symptoms, you might want to consider getting your hearing tested by an audiologist. Audiologists can help determine if you have hearing loss and recommend appropriate treatments, such as hearing aids, cochlear implants, or assistive listening devices to help improve your hearing.
How much do hearing aids cost?
The price of hearing aids can vary widely depending on many factors such as the brand, style, technology level, and features. The more features a hearing aid has, the higher the price.

Another factor that could affect the cost of hearing aids is the location, the type of hearing care professional you work with, and whether or not you have insurance. Some insurance plans may cover a portion of the cost, while others may not cover any of it.

If you're interested in purchasing hearing aids, we recommend consulting with an audiologist. Our friendly staff and audiologists at Hearing Solutions of North Carolina can help walk you through the hearing aid selection and purchasing process.
What is the best hearing aid?

Hearing aids come in many different styles, brands, and technology. Since hearing loss is unique for each individual, it’s impossible to name “the best” hearing aid. Realistically speaking, the best hearing aid will depend on an individual’s unique type and degree of hearing loss, budget, personal preferences, and lifestyle. The best thing you can do is to consult with an audiologist, who can carry out a hearing test and from there, recommend the ideal hearing aid for your hearing requirements.
